questions.question: Define infant mortality rate and calculate it for a district with 6 000 live births and 150 infant deaths.
questions.expected_answer: The number of deaths of infants under one year old per 1 000 live births in a year. 150 / 6 000 x 1 000 = 25 per thousand live births.

questions.question: Give three causes of infant deaths in poorer communities and three ways to prevent them.
questions.expected_answer: Causes: complications around birth and prematurity; diarrhoea from contaminated water and poor sanitation; pneumonia and respiratory infections; malnutrition; malaria; HIV transmission from mother to child. Prevention: trained birth attendants and antenatal care; clean water and sanitation; oral rehydration solution; breastfeeding; immunisation; mosquito nets; antiretroviral treatment for HIV-positive mothers; education of mothers; child support grants.

questions.question: Explain what life expectancy is and describe the changes in South Africa's life expectancy since the 1990s.
questions.expected_answer: Life expectancy at birth is the average number of years a newborn can expect to live if current death rates continue. In South Africa it was about 62 in the early 1990s, fell to about 53 around 2005 because of the HIV and AIDS epidemic, rose to about 65 with the large-scale provision of free antiretroviral treatment from 2004, dipped during COVID-19 and recovered, with women living about five years longer than men.
